questions: Do the iteration 2 race metrics differ from iterations 0 and 1? If they match exactly again, please check whether the race data is a repeat of an earlier run.
With 16 mm footprints, does the sensor signal saturate or dead-zone at the bends, and does the steering still respond cleanly?
At what progress point does the robot first leave the line (early start, mid-track, or at a specific bend)? This tells me whether the failure is sensing or steering response.
Does steering_oscillation rise with the larger footprint, and does this point to the forward lead (y = 0.05 m) as the next change?

intent: Test whether a larger 16 mm sensor footprint, on the ±0.03 m spread, lets the robot keep tape in view past the current drift point and reduces early line loss. Keep the lead at y = 0.05 m and all body and wheel values fixed so the result isolates footprint size. Expect line_loss_events to fall and max_error to stay below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom.
learning: Iteration 1 produced identical metrics to iteration 0, so the spread from ±0.02 m to ±0.03 m is not the limiting factor, or the data is duplicated. Next I want to learn whether footprint size changes the early drift point, and whether the failure starts at the beginning of the course. Please report per-step telemetry for at least one trial per track so I can locate the first departure from the line.
rationale: Iteration 1 changed the sensor spread from ±0.02 m to ±0.03 m, but its race metrics match iteration 0 to four decimal places on all three tracks (max_error 0.0614, 0.0611, 0.0609; progress 0.115, 0.04, 0.035; identical score 26.0449). Either widening the spread had no effect on the robot's behaviour, or the iteration 1 race data duplicates iteration 0. Under either reading, sensor spread alone is not the binding limit, so I will not widen it further. The failure is early on every track (progress 0.035 to 0.115), and the robot leaves the 0.06 m off-track band about 1 line-loss event in, which suggests a fixed drift or steering-response problem near the start. Within geometry, the most direct lever left is the sensor footprint. Moving from 12 mm to 16 mm extends tape visibility by about 2 mm per side at every sensor, so the outer sensors keep reading the tape a little further out before a line loss. I keep the ±0.03 m spread so the change is isolated to footprint size. I keep the body, wheels and mass fixed. Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward zero and max_error drops below the 0.06 m limit on at least the s-bend and slalom. If the metrics again match iterations 0 and 1 exactly, the next step is to verify the race data pipeline, not to change geometry.
